uncited: *   **Baked Volume Texture:** A 3D texture where each voxel stores pre-computed lighting attenuation factors.
The resolution is typically low, matching the base cloud volume resolution.
**Bake Shadow:** Pre-march a shadow ray through the volume for each voxel.
This involves casting rays in the direction of the light source(s) to determine occlusion.
*   *Detail:* Due to the low volume resolution, this can be done in real-time during the baking phase.
**Bake Ambient Occlusion:** Pre-march ambient occlusion rays into the volume texture.
**Runtime Lookup:** During rendering, retrieve the volumetric cloud shadow using a single `tex3D` lookup on the baked texture.
*   **Static Assumption:** This method relies on the volume being static.
*   **Time Complexity:** Baking time is proportional to the number of voxels times the number of shadow/AO samples.
Runtime cost is O(1) per voxel for texture lookup.
*   **Memory Complexity:** O(N) where N is the number of voxels, for storing shadow and AO textures.
*   **When to Use:** Static volumetric clouds where high-quality shadows and AO are desired without runtime cost.
*   **When Not to Use:** Dynamic volumes where geometry changes frequently.
The technique leverages the low resolution of cloud volumes to make pre-marching feasible.
